label: Bible Study
prompt: Before I formed thee in the _____ I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.
verse: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.
note: Jeremiah's call — known before he was formed; the KJV says 'belly' first and 'womb' second.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Now the God of _____ fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
verse: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
note: Paul calls Him 'the God of hope' and prays you'll abound in it — overflowing, not just getting by.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was _____ and wild honey.
verse: And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey.
note: John the Baptist's wardrobe and menu: camel's hair, a leathern girdle, and locusts with wild honey.

label: Deep Water
prompt: For now we see through a glass, _____; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.
verse: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.
note: Corinth was famous for its bronze, mirrors included — Paul says our clearest view now is still a blurry reflection.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the _____ of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
verse: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
note: A shout, the archangel's voice, and 'the trump of God' — the KJV keeps the old short form of trumpet.
